$comment: Single source of truth for which folders/files belong to which sellable edition.
4 buckets: shared (infra, always included, must never import UP into core/pro/premium),
core ⊂ pro ⊂ premium (each tier export includes shared + itself + everything below it).
Consumed by eslint.tier-boundaries.mjs (import-boundary lint) and scripts/export-tier.ts.
Known non-bugs (do not 'fix' by moving these): some folders intentionally hold Core-tier
capability today even though a sibling folder holds the Pro/Premium upgrade of the same
entity, because the underlying features are already split into separate folders:
- app/admin/warehouses (Core: single location) vs app/api/stock-transfers (Pro: transfers)
- app/admin/invoices (Core: manual PDF) vs lib/stripe + app/api/payments (Pro: online pay)
Where a folder can't be split cleanly yet (e.g. app/admin/user-management needs Core's
2-fixed-roles UI now and Pro's custom-role composer later in the SAME folder), that's a
signal for a future feature milestone to split the folder — not a manifest bug to fix now.
middleware/authMiddleware.ts is confirmed-dead legacy code (superseded by proxy.ts) —
bucketed as shared for now since it's harmless, flagged here as a deletion candidate.
KNOWN REAL GAP, unlike the two 'non-bugs' above — proven by `pnpm export:core` then, from
the output dir, `pnpm install && npx tsc --noEmit` (or symlink node_modules for a faster,
install-free check) — not theoretical. A first pass fixed the cleanly-mis-bucketed cases:
components/supplier moved core, lib/payments/order-payment-from-amounts.ts moved to
lib/invoices/order-payment-sync.ts (pure money-math, no Stripe import — was just mis-homed),
the 3 lib/server/support-ticket*-data.ts files moved into lib/support-tickets/,
types/catalog-insights.ts moved core (a core-shaped type with one optional Pro field —
lib/server/product-insights.ts had it computing that Pro field inline too; stopped doing
that and let the already-existing lib/insights/product-insights-enrich.ts wrapper own it,
same pattern lib/server/catalog-insights.ts already used), and
app/api/products/import/route.ts relocated to app/api/products-import/route.ts (out from
under core-bucketed app/api/products) with ProductImportDialog's fetch URL updated to match
— its hideImport gating prop already existed, no new UI pattern needed. Warehouse stock
summary (app/admin/warehouses/page.tsx) also fixed: dropped the blocking SSR
getWarehouseStockSummary call, left it to the existing client-side useWarehouseStockSummary
hook (already undefined-tolerant).
RESOLVED (2026-08-27, Phases 9-11) via the 'per-tier file variant' capability
(Foo.core.tsx/Foo.pro.tsx siblings, export-tier.ts picks one, falling back down the tier
chain when only a .core. variant exists — see export-tier.ts's own header comment):
- Stripe checkout-return SSR reconciliation: app/admin/invoices/[id], app/admin/orders/[id],
app/orders/[id] all have .core.tsx route variants dropping reconcileStripeReturnBeforeDetail;
AdminOrderDetailContent.tsx (relocated core->components/orders, Phase 10) and
OrderDetailPage.tsx/InvoiceDetailPage.tsx have paired .core./.pro. variants dropping
useStripeCheckoutReturn + the components/shipping / components/payments usage.
- components/Pages/ProductDetailPage.tsx: down to 2 real Pro/Premium imports (not six -- the
other 4 named below were mis-bucketed leaf files, relocated into core lib/catalog/ in
Phase 8). Has paired .core./.pro. variants dropping lib/forecasting/entity-forecast and
components/product-reviews/ProductReviewsSection.
- lib/server/forecasting-data.ts relocated -> lib/forecasting/forecasting-data.ts (its only
live caller, app/admin/dashboard-overall-insights/page.tsx, has paired .core./.pro.
variants dropping the forecasting fetch). The 'EIGHT core-bucketed pages' this used to
warn about no longer exists as a caller list -- confirmed via repo-wide grep before fixing;
getCachedForecastingSummary (named below) doesn't exist anywhere in the repo either --
a prior cleanup already dropped that 8-page fan-out, this note just hadn't caught up.
- lib/forecasting/category-forecast-rollup.ts (Category/Supplier/WarehouseDetailPage) has
paired .core./.pro. variants, same pattern.
- lib/server/product-reviews-detail-data.ts relocated -> lib/product-reviews/ (Phase 12,
2026-08-27), fixing its own @/prisma/product-review leak. The feared cascade into
lib/server/order-review-context-data.ts turned out much smaller than it looked: that file
STAYS in lib/server (a premium-bucketed home would make it invisible to Core/Pro exports
entirely, since export-tier.ts only walks a bucket's manifest entries for tiers that include
that bucket) and got .core.ts/.pro.ts stub variants (empty reviews, `eligible: false` for
every product) instead. Because the variant swap happens transparently at that one file's
identity, NONE of its 7 order/invoice-route callers or its 3 downstream
type-only consumers (OrderItemsCard.tsx, InvoiceItemsCard.tsx, ProductLineItemsList.tsx)
needed to change. Also found and fixed in the same pass: ProductLineItemsList.tsx (in
components/shared, used by both core order/invoice cards AND premium
components/shipping/ShippingManagement.tsx -- genuinely cross-tier, not a relocation
candidate) directly rendered the premium ProductReviewsSection per line item; now has
paired .core./.pro. variants too. Also: app/invoices/[id]/page.tsx never got a .core.tsx
Stripe-reconciliation variant in Phase 9 unlike its 3 siblings -- added.
Still open — genuinely hard, not mechanical, deliberately not rushed:
- ProductLineItemsList.tsx's 2 shared->core warnings: RESOLVED (Phase 17, 2026-08-28). Both
were pure/leaf with zero core-only dependency, so this was a relocation, not a variant:
lib/orders/proportional-line-amount.ts -> lib/proportional-line-amount.ts (root-level shared
file, matching the lib/utils.ts precedent); ProductThumb extracted out of
components/products/ProductOptionRow.tsx into components/shared/ProductThumb.tsx (17 of
ProductOptionRow.tsx's 21 importers wanted only ProductThumb -- including 3 files ALREADY in
components/shared/ carrying the same undiscovered warning; the other 5 use the fuller
ProductOptionRow/DialogProductOptionRow row components and correctly stay core-bucketed).
Noted, not fixed: lib/server/*-detail-data.ts carry several other pre-existing shared->core
warnings (prisma/category, prisma/supplier, lib/products/*, lib/orders/order-*) unrelated to
this phase's scope -- see out/phases/phase-17-*.md.
- types/index.ts barrel purity: RESOLVED (Phase 15, 2026-08-28). Added types/index.core.ts
(drops all 11 pro/premium blocks) and types/index.pro.ts (drops the 7 premium-only
blocks, keeps the 4 pro ones as of Phase 15: history, payment, system-config, audit-log --
audit-log itself was reclassified core in Phase 16, see below, so types/index.core.ts
carries that block too now) -- picked up automatically by export-tier.ts's per-tier
variant mechanism, no caller path changes. Surfaced a much bigger, separate finding in
doing so correctly (see immediately below) -- do not re-read this as "barrel fixed, types
area done."
- app/api/orders/[id]/route.ts -> prisma/audit-log coupling: RESOLVED (Phase 16,
2026-08-28), and turned out much broader than the single-file finding filed at Phase 10 --
9 core-bucketed API routes (categories, invoices, invoices/[id], orders, orders/[id],
products, suppliers, users, users/[id], warehouses) all call createAuditLog fire-and-forget
for basic audit trail, all broken the same way. Fixed by reclassifying types/audit-log.ts
and prisma/audit-log.ts core (createAuditLog is core-tier value every route needs; only
getAuditLogs, the browse/filter query behind the Pro-gated app/api/audit-logs viewing
route, is the real Pro feature) and adding prisma/audit-log.core.ts -- a real createAuditLog,
no getAuditLogs. Same transparent-variant shape as order-review-context-data.ts (Phase 12):
Pro/Premium keep the default full file (no .pro.ts needed), none of the 9 calling routes
changed. Verified: Core error count 280->266, Pro unchanged at 165 (default file still
correct), full-repo tsc and check:manifest clean.
- ~56 Core-bucketed files depend directly on a pro/premium type re-exported through
"@/types" with NO tier-gating (support tickets, product reviews, history/audit log,
system config, client/supplier portal dashboards, forecasting, plus lib/api/client.ts
touching nearly all of them) -- invisible to `tsc --noEmit` before Phase 15 for the exact
same reason as the hooks/queries finding below: TypeScript typed the barrel's broken
relative re-exports as `any` instead of cascading "no exported member" to importers
(proven by the pre-fix Core baseline, captured before writing the two variants, having
zero TS2305/TS2724 errors against "@/types" -- 111 of them appear immediately after the
split, 169->280 total; same pattern at Pro scale, 77->165). This finding and the
hooks/queries one below overlap heavily in file list (e.g. AdminSupportTicketDetailContent.tsx,
AdminProductReviewDetailContent.tsx appear in both) -- they are the same ungated features,
just two technical symptoms (a broken hook import and a broken type import) of one "core
shell, premium content, no split" gap. Full breakdown in out/phases/phase-15-*.md; filed
as new backlog Phase 19 (out/ims_progress.md) -- whoever scopes it should treat it and
Phase 18 as one combined per-feature effort, not two separate passes over the same files.
UPDATE (Phase 18, 2026-08-28): the components/admin folder-reclassification fix below
resolved the overlapping admin-file portion of this too (same files, both symptoms) --
down to ~36 files now, mostly lib/server/*, components/Pages/*, lib/api/client.ts (still the
single largest remaining offender at ~25 members in one file). See phase-18-*.md.
- hooks/queries/index.ts barrel purity: RESOLVED (Phase 14, 2026-08-28). Removed the 13
pro/premium re-export lines, repointed all 45 real caller files to each hook's concrete
path. Surfaced a much bigger, separate finding in doing so correctly (see immediately
below) -- do not re-read this as "barrel fixed, hooks/queries area done."
- ~30 Core-bucketed files (components + 2 lib files) depend directly on one of the 13
pro/premium hooks/queries features (product reviews, support tickets, client/supplier
portal dashboards, stock allocation, email preferences, history, admin counts, system
config) with NO tier-gating -- invisible to `tsc --noEmit` before Phase 14 because
TypeScript silently typed the barrel's broken re-export as `any` instead of cascading an
error to importers (proven by reverting hooks/queries/index.ts + one caller to their
pre-session content inside a Core export and re-checking -- zero errors under the old
barrel, same file, same missing feature). This was never real safety: Next.js's bundler
still has to resolve the missing module at build time regardless of what tsc's leniency
hid. Same class of gap as ProductDetailPage.tsx/AdminOrderDetailContent.tsx (core shell,
premium content, no split) but at ~30-file scale -- PARTIALLY RESOLVED (Phase 18,
2026-08-28, see below): the product-reviews and support-tickets admin groups (8 files) and
2 of the 7 client/supplier-portal-dashboard files were a bigger root cause than a missing
variant -- see below. ~18 files remain (stock allocation, the other 5 client/supplier-portal
list components, email-preferences, system-config, admin-counts, ProductActions.tsx),
grouped by feature area in out/phases/phase-14-*.md AND phase-18-*.md for whoever scopes
the follow-up. Fixing even one remaining group properly is its own component-splitting
project.
- components/admin folder-level mis-bucketing: RESOLVED (Phase 18, 2026-08-28). The whole
components/admin folder was ONE bare shared-bucket manifest entry (no per-file overrides),
so all 45 files -- including clearly premium-only admin screens like
AdminSupportTicketDetailContent.tsx -- were physically copied into every Core/Pro export
even though their consuming routes (app/admin/support-tickets, product-reviews,
client-portal, supplier-portal, activity-history, my-activity) were already correctly
pro/premium-bucketed. This -- not a missing hook/type variant -- was the real reason those
files kept erroring. Traced every file's full import chain and reclassified 18 -> premium,
9 -> pro (both confirmed reachable ONLY from already-gated routes); 18 stay shared,
3 of which (ForecastingSection.tsx, SystemConfigSettings.tsx, AdminProductsContent.tsx)
have real internal pro/premium coupling left as a coupled follow-up (their shared parent
unconditionally renders them -- reclassifying the child alone would break the parent's own
export). Added components/admin to check-tier-manifest-coverage.ts's FOLDER_LEVEL_DIRS
(mirroring the existing components/Pages special-case) so each file needs individual
classification going forward. Pure manifest change, no code touched. Resolved a large
overlapping slice of BOTH the hooks finding above AND the ~56-file types finding below at
once (same 27 files carried both symptoms): Core errors 266->193, Pro 165->106. Also
surfaced a new, smaller finding: 6 shared->core eslint warnings in the remaining 18 shared
files (AdminCombinedInvoicesContent/OrdersContent/ProductsContent/WarehousesContent reaching
into their core-bucketed List components, AdminUserManagementDetailContent -> orders/detail,
plus the already-known SystemConfigSettings -> use-system-config) -- not investigated
further, see out/phases/phase-18-*.md.
- 4 more read-only feature hooks reclassified pro/premium -> core: RESOLVED (Phase 19,
2026-08-28). hooks/queries/use-stock-allocation.ts (pro->core -- Core's OWN existing UI,
WarehouseDetailPage.core.tsx's AllocateStockDialog/TransferStockDialog usage, already
depends on it, confirming Phase 13's finding that Core genuinely supports multi-row stock
allocation); hooks/queries/use-portal.ts + types/portal.ts (premium->core together --
client/supplier self-view WITHIN the shared order/invoice/product lists is core-tier,
distinct from the dedicated /client, /supplier, admin client-portal/supplier-portal apps
which stay premium via their OWN separate use-client-portal.ts/use-supplier-portal.ts/
types/client-portal.ts/types/supplier-portal.ts, untouched); hooks/queries/use-admin-counts.ts
and hooks/queries/use-email-preferences.ts (pro->core, trivial -- their types were already
core/shared). All 4 verified safe the same way: zero remaining pro/premium-only dependency
in the file itself, and provably needed by an already-shared/core caller. Pure manifest +
2 barrel-file edits (types/index.core.ts + index.pro.ts needed the portal block back --
Phase 15 had dropped it from both on the wrong assumption it was premium-only), zero
application code changed. Core errors 193->125, Pro 106->64 -- combined with Phase 18,
Core is down 280->125 and Pro 165->64 since Phases 14/15 first surfaced these counts. See
out/phases/phase-19-*.md for the still-open remainder (system config, forecasting, product
reviews, lib/api/client.ts -- each needs a real variant pair or split, not a reclassification)
and for a fuller count (7 more files) of the already-accepted lib/stock-allocation debt below.
- System config + forecasting variant pairs: RESOLVED (Phase 20, 2026-08-28). System config IS
genuinely Pro-only content (unlike Phase 19's reclassifications) -- gave AdminSettingsContent.tsx
a .core.tsx variant (upsell placeholder instead of <SystemConfigSettings>) and reclassified
SystemConfigSettings.tsx + app/api/system-config pro (now orphaned in Core, same 'orphan
removal' as Phase 18); split lib/server/system-config-data.ts and prisma/system-config.ts into
.core.ts variants keeping only the read path (getThemePrimaryColor, called on EVERY page
request by app/layout.tsx's SSR theme injection -- this must keep working in Core) and
dropping the write/seed path. Forecasting was the opposite shape: Core's OWN existing UI
(CategoryDetailPage.core.tsx etc., since Phase 8) already unconditionally used
useForecastingSummary (already core-bucketed); only types/forecasting.ts was still premium --
reclassified core (same barrel-mismatch shape as Phase 19), added AdminAnalyticsContent.core/
pro.tsx (drop the ForecastingSection card, identical to each other) + AdminDashboardMergedView.
core/pro.tsx (drop the now-meaningless initialForecasting prop), reclassified ForecastingSection.tsx
premium (orphaned in both Core and Pro). Core errors 125->83, Pro 64->47.
- IMPORTANT, NOT ACTED ON: investigating forecasting/stock-allocation/portal surfaced that
several hooks now core-bucketed (use-stock-allocation.ts, use-portal.ts, use-forecasting.ts)
call API ROUTES still bucketed pro/premium (app/api/stock-allocations, app/api/stock-transfers,
app/api/portal, app/api/forecasting) -- meaning a real Core deployment's already-shipped UI
would 404 calling them, invisible to both tsc (routes are URL strings) and check:manifest
(bucket coverage only, no cross-route consistency check). This PRE-DATES this whole
engagement -- Phase 19/20 didn't create it, just removed the compile error that was obscuring
it. Whether to move these API routes down a tier is a real product/business decision (moving
a billable backend feature between paid tiers), the same class of call Phase 13 already
established shouldn't be made casually during tier-export hygiene. NOT fixed -- filed as new
Phase 21, see out/ims_progress.md. Whoever picks it up should audit every hook now in the core
bucket against its own API route's bucket, not just the 3 found incidentally here.
- app/api/products/route.ts PUT stock-reconcile mixes a core-relevant guard
(reservedCommitment vs new quantity, using core field Product.reservedQuantity) with
genuinely Pro warehouse-shrink planning (planCatalogQuantityReconcile /
applyCatalogQuantityReconcile against StockAllocation rows) in ONE request handler --
confirmed accurate, not stale (Phase 13, 2026-08-28): the two aren't separable call
sites, they're two fields of ONE input object to ONE pure function
(planCatalogQuantityReconcile), blended into a single reservedCommitment number. A
'Core is single-warehouse, simplify to single-row math' fix was considered and REJECTED
-- no hard single-warehouse constraint exists anywhere in code (verified by grep --
'Core: single location' above is a product-framing convention, not an enforced limit), so
a real Core customer with multiple StockAllocation rows could get silently misallocated
inventory from a naive simplification. A full 2-call split (modeled on the payments
precedent: useCreateCheckout() as a separate follow-up call against an already-created
id) was also considered -- architecturally correct, but changes the request/response
contract for EVERY tier, not just Core (hooks/queries/use-products.ts's
useUpdateProduct() would need to chain two requests) -- a live feature redesign, not
tier-export hygiene. DECISION: accept as documented debt, same class as the directly
comparable prisma/schema note below (lib/products/decrement-stock-allocations.ts) --
investigated and deliberately left alone, not silently skipped. Revisit only if Core's
warehouse feature set changes (e.g. a real single-warehouse constraint gets added).
Don't attempt a real Core sale without re-running the tsc check above and closing every item
it still lists — do not improvise fixes to any of the four above under time pressure.
prisma/schema/ (split multi-file schema, see prisma/schema/schema.prisma's own header) is
bucketed shared IN FULL, not tier-stripped model-by-model, even though each file's header
comment notes which tier's UI primarily owns it. Reason: octalve-ims runs one shared Postgres
database across every tier's codebase, and some Core-tier code has a real dependency on a
Pro-tier model today (lib/products/decrement-stock-allocations.ts reads/writes
StockAllocation for every order, Core included). Stripping prisma/schema/pro-only files out
of a Core export would break that code's `prisma generate` output. Don't split this bucket
without first removing that coupling.
